open_points.subject: public_op:model_fields.model_items
open_points.text: A model's declared fields are the fields its model in the specification lists, each by the name written there and in that order
open_points.question: When the input is an instance of pydantic's BaseModel but its class is not a model listed in the specification, must model_items answer that it is a model and return fields, or answer that it is no model? If it is a model, which field names and order apply when no specification listing exists?
options: Only instances of classes listed in models are models; every other BaseModel instance answers as no model.
Every BaseModel instance is a model; unlisted classes use their Pydantic-declared field names and order.
Every BaseModel instance is a model, but an unlisted class is refused or produces a distinct unsupported-model result.
open_points.default_guess: Follow State 3's BaseModel test: treat every BaseModel instance as a model and use its Pydantic-declared field names and order.

witness.initial: A listed caller holds an instance of a pydantic BaseModel subclass that is not among the specification's models; the public operation admits Any value.
events: module:operations calls module:model_fields.model_items with that value.
outcomes: Because the value is a BaseModel instance, model_items answers its declared name-value pairs.
Because its class has no model listed in the specification, model_items answers that the value is no model.
